samples.summary: Underline toggle-off on a hyperlink becomes a permanent no-op: the guard only knows about named-style defaults, but the painter's link default also keys on `underline === undefined`
Clearing `underline`/`strikethrough` leaves `underlineStyle`/`underlineColor`/`strikeStyle` residue, so the run still cannot re-merge with its neighbour
samples.evidence: BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS covers only the six boolean flags. `inlineStylesEqual` (types.ts:409-412) also compares `underlineStyle`, `underlineColor` and `strikeStyle`. A run that was underlined with a variant (e.g. wavy) and then toggled off keeps `underlineStyle: 'wavy'`, so `normalizeInlines` still cannot merge it with the identical-looking neighbour — the very defect the change claims to fix — and re-enabling underline silently resurrects the old variant. `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` (types.ts:244-246) clears all three together, showing they are meant to travel as a unit.

samples.summary: A kept `false` becomes a dead flag as soon as the block's type changes away from the style that justified it
samples.evidence: The exception branch stores `italic: false` on a Heading 6 run because the named style supplies italic. Nothing re-evaluates that decision when the block is later converted (`setBlockType(blockId, 'paragraph')`, document.ts:447): the run keeps `italic: false` under a style that supplies nothing, which is exactly the dead flag described in the method's own doc comment — unmergeable by `inlineStylesEqual`, and pinned against a later 'Normal text' redefinition to italic. Same for a Heading-6 run copied/pasted into a paragraph.

samples.summary: In the collaborative store the split runs are only merged in the cache, not in the Yorkie tree, so the #749 split-run symptom returns after a reload/remote parse
samples.evidence: `applyStyle` updates the cache with `applyInlineStyleHelper` (line 1707), which runs `normalizeInlines` and merges the now-identical runs, while `applyStyleInTree` only removes the attribute from inline node `i` — no node merge (lines 1884-1890). `treeNodeToBlock` / `treeNodeToInline` (lines 355-363, 390) map tree children 1:1 with no normalization, so any other client, and this client after a reload, still sees three adjacent inlines with identical (empty) styles where the cached doc showed one. The cache and the parsed tree therefore disagree on inline count immediately after a toggle-off.

finding.summary: Underline toggle-off on a hyperlink becomes a permanent no-op: the guard only knows about named-style defaults, but the painter's link default also keys on `underline === undefined`

verdict.reason: Every claimed location verified. `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:399-418) rewrites `underline: false` to `undefined` unless the block's NAMED style supplies the key (line 413); `underline` is in BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS (document.ts:42) and no named style sets underline (no matches for `underline` in model/named-styles.ts). The write path really deletes the key: store.applyStyle (memory.ts:213-216) -> applyInlineStyle -> mergeInlineStyle `if (patch[key] === undefined) delete merged[key]` (block-helpers.ts:322). The painter has a second, href-keyed implicit default the guard never consults: `let showUnderline = style.underline ?? false; if (style.href) { ... if (style.underline === undefined) showUnderline = true; }` (paint-layout.ts:387-391). Links never store an explicit `underline: true` — insertLink writes only `{ href: url }` (editor.ts:2955/2962/2981/2997, text-box-editor.ts:1189/1207/1221). So underline-off on a link deletes the key and the painter re-underlines: a permanent visual no-op. The read side compounds it: visitStyledRunsInRange merges only named-style defaults (range-runs.ts:57-64), which feeds toggleStyle's add-vs-remove decision (text-editor.ts:2879-2893), so the summary reports OFF for a run that paints underlined and the toggle oscillates between `true` and key-deleted, never removing the underline. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable — the only href-aware underline logic is in the painter itself.

finding.summary: Clearing a boolean key can make an image run byte-identical to an adjacent identical image run, and `normalizeInlines` (unlike the paste path) merges structural inlines — losing one image
finding.evidence: `normalizeInlines` (block-helpers.ts:76-86) merges any two adjacent runs for which `inlineStylesEqual` is true, with **no** `isStructuralInline` guard. `inlineStylesEqual` compares images through `imageDataEqual` (types.ts:383-398), i.e. two *identical* images (copy/paste an image beside itself) compare equal — exactly the case types.ts:432-436 and TextEditor.normalizeInlineList (view/text-editor.ts:3722, issue #726) say must never merge. Before this change a toggle-off wrote `bold: false` onto the styled image run, which differed from its unstyled twin and kept them split; now `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:399-418) rewrites it to `undefined` and `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325) *deletes* the key, so run A's style becomes exactly `{image}` — equal to twin B. `applyInlineStyle` ends with `normalizeInlines(newInlines)` (line 380), which concatenates them into one 2-character run under a single `style.image`: the second image is dropped from the model while the offsets still count both characters (layout emits one image segment for the 2-char inline). Repro: two adjacent identical images, image A bolded, B not; select only A and press Cmd+B (summary reads bold-on for that run, so the toggle sends `bold:false`).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: `normalizeInlines` (store/block-helpers.ts:76-86) merges adjacent runs purely on `inlineStylesEqual` with no `isStructuralInline` guard, while the sibling implementation in view/text-editor.ts:3712-3730 does guard exactly this case citing #726. `inlineStylesEqual` (model/types.ts:404-424) compares images via `imageDataEqual` (types.ts:383-399), a field-wise comparison, so two byte-identical images compare equal — the very case types.ts:426-440 documents as "must still stay separate runs" because concatenation yields a 2-char run under one `style.image` and silently drops the second image. The clear path is present as claimed: Document.applyInlineStyle (document.ts:375-380) routes through styleOffAsClear (document.ts:399-418), which rewrites a toggled-off boolean `false` to `undefined` when the named style doesn't supply it, and mergeInlineStyle (block-helpers.ts:316-325) deletes such keys, so a de-bolded image run's style collapses back to exactly `{image}` and becomes equal to its unstyled twin; applyInlineStyle then calls normalizeInlines at block-helpers.ts:380 (reached from MemoryStore.applyStyle, store/memory.ts:213-216). The precondition state is creatable: paste writes inlines via spliceInlinesAt/normalizeInlineList (text-editor.ts:3556, 3574, 3603), which intentionally preserves two identical adjacent image runs. No guard anywhere in model/document.ts excludes structural inlines from inline-style application (grep for isStructuralInline/style.image in document.ts finds none), so nothing prevents the merge. Reachable data loss (image dropped from the model while offsets still count its character) — critical in the correctness lane.

mergedFrom.summary: Every B/I/U/S toggle-off now emits a `removeStyleByPath` op instead of a `styleByPath` set; concurrent-edit resolution between remove-attribute and set-attribute ops is not the same LWW path the old `bold=false` write used

finding.summary: Every style write, including the now-hot pure-clear toggle-off, re-asserts the node's full existing attribute map, which can clobber a concurrent remote attribute change
finding.evidence: `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], { ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs })` re-sends every attribute already on the node even when `styleAttrs` is empty (the pure-clear case `{bold: undefined}` that, per the comment added at lines 1873-1875, is now every B/I/U/S toggle-off). The comment two lines above states styleByPath 'only merges', so passing `existingAttrs` is unnecessary; because it is sent with a fresh local timestamp, an LWW-per-attribute Tree resolves it over a concurrent peer's change to an unrelated attribute (e.g. peer sets `color` while this client toggles bold off), reverting the peer's edit. The delta puts this redundant full-attribute rewrite on the hottest editing path.

verdict.reason: The cited code is present verbatim: yorkie-doc-store.ts:1885-1886 reads `inlines[i].attributes` and sends `{ ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs }` through `tree.styleByPath` on every inline in the styled range, unconditionally. The supporting context the finding relies on also checks out: `serializeInlineStyle` (lines 107-133) drops keys whose value is `undefined`, `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (lines 144-163) routes them to `removeStyleByPath`, and the in-file comment at 1871-1881 plus docs/tasks/active/20260819-docs-inline-style-off-clears-key-todo.md:31-40 confirm that after #749 every B/I/U/S toggle-off arrives as an explicit `undefined`, i.e. `styleAttrs` is `{}` and the styleByPath write consists solely of a re-assertion of the node's pre-existing attributes — on the hottest editing path. No guard or caller-side filter prevents this path (reached via applyStyleInTree from applyStyle/applyStyles, e.g. line 1760), and the file's own comment that styleByPath "only merges" shows `existingAttrs` is not load-bearing for the local result, so the write is redundant. I could not read Yorkie's tree attribute resolution (no node_modules/vendored SDK present) to independently confirm the LWW-per-attribute clobber of a concurrent peer write; under standard Yorkie tree RHT semantics the described peer-edit revert follows, and that residual uncertainty keeps the finding rather than refuting it. Overwriting a peer's committed attribute is data overwrite / broken convergence invariant, squarely in the correctness lane, so no out-of-scope ground applies.

finding.summary: Yorkie tree write ignores the superscript/subscript mutual exclusion that the cache write applies, so the CRDT keeps both flags while the local cache shows one
finding.evidence: `applyStyle` (line 1707) updates the cache with `applyInlineStyleHelper(block, from, to, style)`, and that helper (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:337-343) resolves `{superscript:true}` into `{superscript:true, subscript:undefined}` and, via `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325), *deletes* `subscript` from the run. The tree path (`applyStyleInTree`, line 1716) is handed the RAW `style`: `serializeInlineStyle(style)` at line 1882 emits only `superscript:'true'` and `removedInlineStyleAttrs(style)` at line 1883 returns `[]` because `subscript` is not a key of the patch. Since `styleByPath` only merges, the pre-existing `subscript='true'` attribute survives on the Tree node. Ctrl+. on subscripted text (text-editor.ts:899) therefore leaves the CRDT with both `superscript` and `subscript` set; `parseInlineStyle` (line 168-173) reads both back on reload or on any remote-driven cache invalidation, so the run silently changes appearance/state relative to what the user saw. This is exactly the 'styleByPath cannot delete' class of bug the surrounding comment block (lines 1871-1881) claims is handled on this path.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `applyStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1707) applies the mutual-exclusion-resolving cache helper (block-helpers.ts:337-343 + mergeInlineStyle 316-325, which deletes undefined keys) but passes the RAW `style` to `applyStyleInTree` (line 1716; same split in `applyStyles` 1760 vs 1770). Inside `applyStyleInTree`, `serializeInlineStyle` (line 1882, helper 100-113) emits only defined keys, and `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (line 1883, helper 144-163) only removes keys explicitly present-and-undefined, so a `{superscript:true}` patch produces no `subscript` removal and `styleByPath`'s merge (line 1886) leaves the old `subscript='true'` attribute on the node. A live caller supplies exactly that one-key patch: text-editor.ts:899 `toggleStyle({superscript:true})` → toggleStyle only rewrites keys present in the patch (2880-2893) → Document.applyInlineStyle → styleOffAsClear, which only maps false→undefined and never adds the opposite key (document.ts:399-418). `parseInlineStyle` (172-173) then reads both flags back on reload/remote sync, so the CRDT and local cache diverge. No guard exists anywhere on this path; docs-view.tsx:322 wires YorkieDocStore to the docs editor, so it is reachable. Real correctness bug (state divergence / broken invariant) in the Correctness lane.
